provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In the original task, objects fall downward. The D4 transform changes that direction as follows. A row reversal (d4>=4) mirrors horizontally, so it leaves the vertical fall direction unchanged. Each clockwise rotation turns the fall direction from down to left, then up, then right. The factory therefore sets a visible fall vector (DR, DC) from d4%4. It also fixes the colour roles as palette constants: BG=palette[8], LINE=palette[2] and OBJ=palette[1].

The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates:
- It finds the full line of LINE colour that is perpendicular to the fall axis.
- It finds the 4-connected OBJ components and erases all of them.
- For each object, it groups cells into slices perpendicular to the fall direction. A slice is a row for vertical falls and a column for horizontal falls.
- If no slice has more than one cell (a width-1 object), the object slides along the fall direction until its leading cell touches the grid edge. The line cell in its lane becomes BG, leaving a hole.
- Otherwise, the program takes the wide slice nearest the fall direction and places it in the slice just before the line. Any thin stem beyond it overlaps the line and turns those line cells OBJ, because objects are drawn after the holes are punched.

This matches the constructor. Its hole on the line is overwritten by the stem for caught objects with a thin bottom, and caught objects with a wide bottom leave the line intact.
draft_notes.limitations:
- Direction and colour roles come from d4 and palette, not from the demonstrations. The program assumes the episode was generated by this constructor under the stated D4/palette convention.
- Line detection looks for a fully uniform LINE row or column along the expected axis. If none exists, it falls back to the row or column with the most LINE cells.
- The archived solver can flip the grid when objects start below the line, but the constructor never produces that case, so it is not reproduced. Objects always start on the side opposite the fall direction.
- Objects are assumed to be 4-connected single-colour components that are separated from each other. The constructor guarantees this with a gap of at least one column.
- No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found. Width-1 objects never land on the line, because max_tall <= size-line-2, and the stems of caught objects stay inside the grid.
- Untested by me; the host must verify.
